newsitem.title: NIGER: Another technocrat to head new Niger government.
newsitem.headline: Another technocrat to head new Niger government.

text.p: Niger's President Ibrahim Bare Mainassara dropped Prime Minister Boukary Adji on Saturday and appointed another technocrat to head a new government marking a fresh start at democracy in the West African nation.
An official statement said Finance Minister Ahmadou Boubacar Cisse, 48, a former World Bank staffer, would take over as prime minister in a 27-member cabinet that included three women.

He takes over from Adji, a former governor of the Central Bank of West African States who was appointed after Mainassara, then army chief, took power in a coup last January 27, toppling Niger's Third Republic civilian government.
Following the coup, condemned by Niger's Western creditors, Mainassara stood in presidential elections in July and was declared winner after controversial voting denounced by the United States.
He locked up his opponents and dismissed the electoral commission mid-way in balloting. A handpicked commission declared him elected.
The political party supporting Mainassara swept an overwhelming majority of seats in subsequent legislative elections boycotted by the opposition.

Mainassara last week dissolved the military council through which he has ruled the impoverished nation since seizing power in the wake of a long stand-off between the civilian president and his prime minister, who was from a different party.
In the new government, Foreign Minister Andre Salifou has been reassigned the portfolio of Minister of State charged with relations with the National Assembly.
The new foreign minister is Ibrahim Hassane Mayaki.

The prime minister looks certain to keep some control of the economy and finance as two key economic portfolios have been created at junior minister level in his office, one of them with responsibility for privatisation.
The government includes a total of five new faces.
